notes: Shared vectors for the Notes Markdown profile on web (TypeScript) and Android (Kotlin). The profile is docs/contributing/notes-markdown.md.

Each case has an id, a since tag (commonmark or gfm), the Markdown text, and an expect object that each client compares with the result of its own renderer. The fields are defined on the profile page.
Characters that are hard to see (controls, bidi overrides, lone surrogates) are written as escapes so the exact code units are in the file.

cases.note: Nested inline spans are listed in the order their opening markers appear, outer span first.

cases.markdown:
- a
  - b
    1. c
- d

1. x
2. y
cases.note: Only top-level blocks are listed; nested content is checked through text.
A single newline is a soft break: no line break element.
Frontmatter is not interpreted in 1.0: the first line is a thematic break and the next two lines with the closing dashes form a setext heading.
table:RxC counts the header row in R.
The definition line produces no block.
The scheme is compared without regard to case; the target is kept exactly as written.
Bare URLs are not links in 1.0 (decided in PR 1 of the profile).
Percent escapes are not decoded for the scheme check: a target that does not start with the scheme itself is relative, so not live.
Raw HTML is literal text. The html block kind means a block shown as literal text.
A link text does not count image placeholders.
The parser decodes the entity, so the target is javascript: before the scheme check.
Browsers strip a tab inside a scheme; the decoded target does not start with an allowed scheme, so it is not live.
A tab is not allowed in an inline destination, so this is not a link at all; nothing may become live either way.
A valid CommonMark autolink by syntax; shown as its text, not live.
react-markdown 10.1.0 allows irc, ircs and xmpp by default; the profile does not.
The profile does not change link text: bidi controls are kept. Known limit, see the page.
Known limit: the profile does not compare link text with its target.
100 levels on one line must render as Markdown.

cases.note: Each line is indented two columns deeper than the one before: 100 levels over 100 lines must render as Markdown, like 100 markers on one line.
blocks is omitted on purpose: past 100 levels a client may degrade (the web shows the whole body as plain text). It must not crash or stall, and the text must stay visible.
Without a cap the web parser needs about 15 seconds for this one line.
A parser skips a leading U+FEFF, so a nesting limit has to skip it too. blocks is omitted: a client may or may not strip it.
U+0000 must not reach the output (CommonMark replaces it with U+FFFD). Lone surrogates must not crash.
